title: Introducing Shieldstral. | Mistral AI
excerpt: Shieldstral introduces a 3B open-weights multimodal safety classifier that outperforms models up to 7x its size.
content_html:
Thinking

Summary

Shieldstral introduces a 3B open-weights multimodal safety classifier that outperforms models up to 7x its size by framing content moderation as a policy-adaptive question-answering task. Unlike traditional guardrail models, it accepts plain-language policies at inference time, unifying text and image safety evaluation without retraining. Released under Apache 2.0, it delivers calibrated safety scores across diverse benchmarks while running efficiently on a single 16GB NVIDIA GPU.

A 3B open-weights, policy-adaptive multimodal safety classifier that matches models up to 7x its size on text safety and sets a new state of the art on multimodal moderation.

“Does this content promote violence against a protected group? Is this image safe to show to a minor? Did the assistant refuse the request?”

Every product that ships a model needs to answer questions like these — but the right answer depends on the product, the audience, and the moment. The same content can be fine for a cybersecurity research tool and harmful on a mental-health platform. Most guardrail models bake a fixed taxonomy of harm categories into their weights, so re-targeting them to a new deployment context means retraining. And because safety definitions differ across applications and domains, there is no single "correct" set of categories to model in the first place.

Shieldstral takes a different approach: you write the policy as a plain-language question at inference time, and the model returns a calibrated safety score. No retraining, one interface for text and images, and a verdict from a single token. Please refer to our technical report here.

As an inaugural member of the Open Secure AI Alliance with NVIDIA and other organizations, today we're releasing Shieldstral as open weights under Apache 2.0, available for download here.

Moderation as a question

Shieldstral frames content moderation as a binary question-answering task. Each request has three parts:

  • <Instruct> — the evaluation context, strictness, and (optionally) a definition of what counts as unsafe content.

  • <Query> — a single yes/no question, e.g. "Does this content promote physical violence?"

  • <Document> — the content to judge: a prompt, a response, a prompt–response pair, or an image with optional text.

At inference the model reads out only the yes and no logits and softmax-normalizes them into a continuous safety score. This one simple formulation does a lot of work: it unifies prompt classification, response moderation, refusal detection, and toxicity detection into a single problem; it lets policies live entirely in the prompt, so one checkpoint adapts to novel policies at deployment time.

Highlights

  • Strong performance — matches or outperforms open guard models up to 7× its size across text safety, refusal detection, policy adaptability, and multimodal benchmarks.

  • Adaptive and flexible — a single natural-language interface covers text, image, and text+image content across prompts, responses, and prompt–response pairs. Policies are supplied as free-form queries and re-targeted at inference time, without retraining.

  • Small, trained on heterogeneous sources — a 3B model that runs on a single 16GB GPU, trained on real and synthetic data with diverse label formats and taxonomies, consolidated into one framework.

  • Continuous safety score — returns a calibrated yes/no probability from a single forward pass, so you can threshold or rank by confidence rather than relying on a discrete label.

  • Open — Apache 2.0 weights.

Benchmarks

We evaluate Shieldstral against open guard models up to 7x its size across four axes. All evaluation samples are held out from training.

How we built it

The core idea is that a small model can beat much larger ones if the data is right. Getting the data right meant solving four problems:

Unify heterogeneous data. Public safety datasets disagree on taxonomies, labels, and annotation conventions — from binary safe/unsafe flags to fine-grained multi-label taxonomies. We convert every dataset into the same instruction–query–document format with a per-dataset processor, and we vary the wording of instructions, queries, and prompt–response delimiters so the model generalizes across phrasing instead of overfitting to one style. We also calibrate strictness per source — strict for adversarial jailbreaks, lenient for response-quality data — so the model learns calibrated decision boundaries. This lets us consolidate sources that would otherwise be incompatible.

Teach discrimination, not memorization. If trained on a fixed set of policy labels, a model learns only to classify those predefined policies, rather than reasoning about the precise boundaries of a given policy. This prevents generalization to novel policies. Instead, we construct sets of deliberately similar, easily confused policies and ask an LLM to rewrite safe text into contrastive pairs: each rewrite is engineered to violate one policy but not its sibling. This trains the model to distinguish which specific policy a piece of content violates, a skill that transfers to unseen, user-defined policies at inference time.

Ground safety in images. Unsafe images can't be synthezised by an LLM the way text can, so visual safety data is scarce. We supplement limited moderation datasets with general-purpose image datasets as high-quality negatives, mutate queries to augment the dataset, and filter every image–query pair through a vision–language reranker to reduce mislabeled data and hallucinations.

Combine complementary checkpoints. We fine-tune with LoRA and merge — via SLERP — a checkpoint calibrated on public data, one that adds fine-grained policy discrimination from generated data, and the base instruct model. The merge recovers common policy calibration and policy adaptability in a single model, and instruction-following from the base model transfers to the moderation task.

Forge. We built Shieldstral end to end on Forge, our platform for training, aligning, and evaluating custom models. Forge managed the infrastructure, data and model sharding, metrics, and logging on top of state-of-the-art distributed training, so the team could stay focused on the data which is what determines the safety model's quality.

What's next

Shieldstral is a step toward moderation that adapts to context instead of forcing every product through one frozen taxonomy. We're continuing to push on multilingual coverage, longer-document robustness, and broader multimodal safety — and we'd love to see what the community builds on top of it.

BTW, we're hiring! If you want to help make AI better, see our careers page.

sentences.en: We convert every dataset into the same instruction–query–document format with a per-dataset processor, and we vary the wording of instructions, queries, and prompt–response delimiters so the model generalizes across phrasing instead of overfitting to one style.
sentences.zh: 我们使用每个数据集处理器将每个数据集转换为相同的指令-查询-文档格式，并且我们改变指令、查询和提示-响应分隔符的措辞，以便模型在措辞上进行概括，而不是过度拟合一种风格。

sentences.en: We also calibrate strictness per source — strict for adversarial jailbreaks, lenient for response-quality data — so the model learns calibrated decision boundaries.
sentences.zh: 我们还校准每个来源的严格性——对对抗性越狱严格，对响应质量数据宽松——因此模型学习校准的决策边界。

sentences.en: This lets us consolidate sources that would otherwise be incompatible.
sentences.zh: 这让我们能够整合原本不兼容的资源。

blocks.html_en: Teach discrimination, not memorization. If trained on a fixed set of policy labels, a model learns only to classify those predefined policies, rather than reasoning about the precise boundaries of a given policy. This prevents generalization to novel policies. Instead, we construct sets of deliberately similar, easily confused policies and ask an LLM to rewrite safe text into contrastive pairs: each rewrite is engineered to violate one policy but not its sibling. This trains the model to distinguish which specific policy a piece of content violates, a skill that transfers to unseen, user-defined policies at inference time.

sentences.en: Teach discrimination, not memorization.
sentences.zh: 教的是辨别力，而不是记忆力。

sentences.en: If trained on a fixed set of policy labels, a model learns only to classify those predefined policies, rather than reasoning about the precise boundaries of a given policy.
sentences.zh: 如果在一组固定的策略标签上进行训练，模型只会学习对这些预定义的策略进行分类，而不是推理给定策略的精确边界。

sentences.en: This prevents generalization to novel policies.
sentences.zh: 这阻碍了新政策的推广。

sentences.en: Instead, we construct sets of deliberately similar, easily confused policies and ask an LLM to rewrite safe text into contrastive pairs: each rewrite is engineered to violate one policy but not its sibling.
sentences.zh: 相反，我们故意构建一组相似的、容易混淆的政策，并要求法学硕士将安全文本重写为对比对：每次重写都旨在违反一项政策，但不违反其同级政策。

sentences.en: This trains the model to distinguish which specific policy a piece of content violates, a skill that transfers to unseen, user-defined policies at inference time.
sentences.zh: 这训练模型来区分一段内容违反了哪个特定策略，这种技能可以在推理时转移到看不见的、用户定义的策略。

blocks.html_en: Ground safety in images. Unsafe images can't be synthezised by an LLM the way text can, so visual safety data is scarce. We supplement limited moderation datasets with general-purpose image datasets as high-quality negatives, mutate queries to augment the dataset, and filter every image–query pair through a vision–language reranker to reduce mislabeled data and hallucinations.

sentences.en: Ground safety in images.
sentences.zh: 图像中的地面安全。

sentences.en: Unsafe images can't be synthezised by an LLM the way text can, so visual safety data is scarce.
sentences.zh: 法学硕士无法像文本那样合成不安全的图像，因此视觉安全数据稀缺。

sentences.en: We supplement limited moderation datasets with general-purpose image datasets as high-quality negatives, mutate queries to augment the dataset, and filter every image–query pair through a vision–language reranker to reduce mislabeled data and hallucinations.
sentences.zh: 我们用通用图像数据集作为高质量底片来补充有限的审核数据集，改变查询以增强数据集，并通过视觉语言重新排序器过滤每个图像查询对，以减少错误标记的数据和幻觉。

blocks.html_en: Combine complementary checkpoints. We fine-tune with LoRA and merge — via SLERP — a checkpoint calibrated on public data, one that adds fine-grained policy discrimination from generated data, and the base instruct model. The merge recovers common policy calibration and policy adaptability in a single model, and instruction-following from the base model transfers to the moderation task.

sentences.en: Combine complementary checkpoints.
sentences.zh: 结合互补的检查点。

sentences.en: We fine-tune with LoRA and merge — via SLERP — a checkpoint calibrated on public data, one that adds fine-grained policy discrimination from generated data, and the base instruct model.
sentences.zh: 我们使用 LoRA 进行微调，并通过 SLERP 合并一个根据公共数据校准的检查点，该检查点从生成的数据和基本指令模型中添加了细粒度的策略区分。

sentences.en: The merge recovers common policy calibration and policy adaptability in a single model, and instruction-following from the base model transfers to the moderation task.
sentences.zh: 合并在单个模型中恢复常见的策略校准和策略适应性，并且指令遵循从基本模型转移到调节任务。

blocks.html_en: Forge. We built Shieldstral end to end on Forge, our platform for training, aligning, and evaluating custom models. Forge managed the infrastructure, data and model sharding, metrics, and logging on top of state-of-the-art distributed training, so the team could stay focused on the data which is what determines the safety model's quality.

sentences.zh: 我们在 Forge 上构建了端到端的 Shieldstral，Forge 是我们用于训练、调整和评估自定义模型的平台。

We're continuing to push on multilingual coverage, longer-document robustness, and broader multimodal safety — and we'd love to see what the community builds on top of it.

content_html_zh:
思维

概括

Shieldstral 引入了 3B 开放权重多模式安全分类器，通过将内容审核构建为策略自适应问答任务，其性能优于其大小高达 7 倍的模型。 与传统的护栏模型不同，它在推理时接受简单语言的策略，统一文本和图像安全评估，无需重新训练。 它在 Apache 2.0 下发布，可在不同的基准上提供经过校准的安全分数，同时在单个 16GB NVIDIA GPU 上高效运行。

3B 开放权重、策略自适应多模态安全分类器，在文本安全性方面匹配高达 7 倍大小的模型，并在多模态调节方面树立了新的技术水平。

“此内容是否宣扬针对受保护群体的暴力行为？ 向未成年人展示此图片是否安全？ 助理拒绝了这个请求吗？”

每个发布模型的产品都需要回答这样的问题——但正确的答案取决于产品、受众和时机。 同样的内容对于网络安全研究工具可能没问题，但对于心理健康平台却有害。 大多数护栏模型将固定的伤害类别分类纳入其权重中，因此将它们重新定位到新的部署环境意味着重新训练。 而且由于安全定义在不同的应用程序和领域中有所不同，因此首先没有一组“正确”的类别可供建模。

Shieldstral 采用不同的方法：您在推理时将策略编写为简单语言问题，模型返回经过校准的安全评分。 无需重新训练，一个文本和图像界面，以及来自单个令牌的判决。 请在此处参阅我们的技术报告。

作为与 NVIDIA 和其他组织合作的开放安全 AI 联盟的创始成员，今天我们将 Shieldstral 作为 Apache 2.0 下的开放权重发布，可在此处下载。

适度作为一个问题

Shieldstral 将内容审核视为一项二元问答任务。 每个请求由三个部分组成：

  • <Instruct> — 评估上下文、严格性和（可选）不安全内容的定义。
  • <Query> — 一个是/否问题，例如“此内容是否宣扬身体暴力？”
  • <Document> — 要判断的内容：提示、响应、提示-响应对或带有可选文本的图像。

在推理时，模型仅读出是和否逻辑，并将它们进行 softmax 归一化为连续的安全评分。 这一简单的表述做了很多工作：它将及时分类、响应调节、拒绝检测和毒性检测统一为一个问题；它让策略完全存在于提示中，因此一个检查点会在部署时适应新的策略。

亮点

  • 强大的性能——在文本安全性、拒绝检测、策略适应性和多模式基准方面，与开放式防护模型相匹配或优于其大小高达 7 倍。
  • 自适应且灵活——单一自然语言界面涵盖提示、响应和提示-响应对中的文本、图像和文本+图像内容。 策略以自由格式查询的形式提供，并在推理时重新定位，无需重新训练。
  • 小型，在异构源上进行训练——一种在单个 16GB GPU 上运行的 3B 模型，对具有不同标签格式和分类法的真实数据和合成数据进行训练，并整合到一个框架中。
  • 连续安全评分 - 从单次前向传递中返回校准的是/否概率，因此您可以按置信度进行阈值或排名，而不是依赖离散标签。
  • 开放 — Apache 2.0 权重。

基准测试

我们针对 Shieldstral 的四个轴尺寸高达 7 倍的开放式防护模型进行了评估。 所有评估样本均来自训练。

我们是如何构建它的

核心思想是，如果数据正确，小模型可以击败大模型。 获得正确的数据意味着解决四个问题：

统一异构数据。 公共安全数据集在分类法、标签和注释约定上存在分歧——从二进制安全/不安全标志到细粒度的多标签分类法。 我们使用每个数据集处理器将每个数据集转换为相同的指令-查询-文档格式，并且我们改变指令、查询和提示-响应分隔符的措辞，以便模型在措辞上进行概括，而不是过度拟合一种风格。 我们还校准每个来源的严格性——对对抗性越狱严格，对响应质量数据宽松——因此模型学习校准的决策边界。 这让我们能够整合原本不兼容的资源。

教的是辨别力，而不是记忆力。 如果在一组固定的策略标签上进行训练，模型只会学习对这些预定义的策略进行分类，而不是推理给定策略的精确边界。 这阻碍了新政策的推广。 相反，我们故意构建一组相似的、容易混淆的政策，并要求法学硕士将安全文本重写为对比对：每次重写都旨在违反一项政策，但不违反其同级政策。 这训练模型来区分一段内容违反了哪个特定策略，这种技能可以在推理时转移到看不见的、用户定义的策略。

图像中的地面安全。 法学硕士无法像文本那样合成不安全的图像，因此视觉安全数据稀缺。 我们用通用图像数据集作为高质量底片来补充有限的审核数据集，改变查询以增强数据集，并通过视觉语言重新排序器过滤每个图像查询对，以减少错误标记的数据和幻觉。

结合互补的检查点。 我们使用 LoRA 进行微调，并通过 SLERP 合并一个根据公共数据校准的检查点，该检查点从生成的数据和基本指令模型中添加了细粒度的策略区分。 合并在单个模型中恢复常见的策略校准和策略适应性，并且指令遵循从基本模型转移到调节任务。

锻造。 我们在 Forge 上构建了端到端的 Shieldstral，Forge 是我们用于训练、调整和评估自定义模型的平台。 Forge 在最先进的分布式训练之上管理基础设施、数据和模型分片、指标和日志记录，因此团队可以专注于决定安全模型质量的数据。

接下来是什么

Shieldstral 是朝着适应环境的适度迈出的一步，而不是强迫每一种产品都通过一个冻结的分类法。 我们正在继续推动多语言覆盖、更长文档的稳健性和更广泛的多式联运安全性——我们很想看看社区在此基础上构建了什么。

顺便说一句，我们正在招聘！ 如果您想帮助改善人工智能，请参阅我们的职业页面。
